symptom: A C++17 project repeatedly failed because the CE public contract used std::chrono::year_month_day, while Director repair added chrono includes and compatibility scaffolding without removing the C++20-only API.
dynamic_evidence: The persisted CE blueprint declared std::chrono::year_month_day in MoonPhase and DiaryEntry public signatures despite the product contract requiring C++17.

The same Director task received the exact failed target and produced a real edit_file effect on include/invisible_ink/moon_phase.hpp with distinct before/after hashes and a committed physical-effect receipt.
The exact verifier rerun still failed on year_month_day not being a member of std::chrono under -std=c++17.
Live query_director_repair_coverage classified the first diagnostic as cpp.standard_include and the second as coverage_gap, proving a contradictory repair route for one physical incompatibility.
root_cause: GCC 12 does not emit an 'only available from C++20' note for std::chrono::year_month_day under C++17. Diagnostic normalization therefore left the error as cpp_compile_error, allowing cpp.standard_include to claim it and steer repair toward ineffective include insertion.
remaining_gate: A fresh isolated run must prove the runtime classifies the C++20-only chrono symbol as cpp_language_standard_incompatibility and does not schedule cpp.standard_include for it.
